plan.hypothesis: Decreasing control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from the source value 0.05 to its domain lower bound 0.025 on the T0-template configuration under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0 will lower holding_max_speed_m_s below the 0.02 m/s acceptance bound while keeping terminal_error_m and holding_max_error_m below 0.01 m, force_bound_violation_n at 0.0 N and a finite valid complete execution, thereby attaining joint nominal reach-and-hold acceptance.
plan.rationale: Control-only research is legitimate and the recipe tip-speed weights are the only legal continuous control paths. The joint failure is a held-speed failure, and terminal_tip_speed_weight is saturated at its 0.1 upper bound, leaving control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight as the usable lever. The source configuration batch-0497cdd238512a92-0 is distinct from the latest tested candidate (batch-67047ea375b20a2c-1) and the retained baseline (fixed-radius), yet sits on the same T0 template, so the comparison isolates the weight change. Because only one development execution remains, a deterministic one-point explicit enumeration at the lower domain bound 0.025 is chosen over an uncontrolled coordinate proposal that could step upward. Every point must produce a complete evaluation with force bounds and a finite valid execution before any claim, and no cross-template routing scale is reapplied.
stopping_conditions: batch backend cap of 1 new attempt reached
weakening_observations: Historical T0-family executions used controller 9.0.0 (F323) while this batch runs controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, so historical metrics may not transfer.
Only two controller10 points vary holding_tip_speed_weight and the observed downward direction is counterintuitive relative to the weight name, so the trend may not extrapolate to 0.025.
No recorded evidence links holding_tip_speed_weight to terminal reach; the required sub-0.01 m terminal error may be structure-limited.
The source point's held speed (~0.0219 m/s) is only ~0.002 m/s above the bound, so the outcome may be sensitive to numerical detail.
T0/T1/T2/T3 differ in independent force capacity, split guide/routing and tension-guess sources, confounding cross-template attribution.
